observations: Large multi-cylinder inline diesel engine block, greenish-gray paint, heavily weathered and rusted in places.
Large flywheel with visible ring gear at the front of the block.
Engine rests on wooden blocks/pallet, sitting on muddy, outdoor ground.
Loose wiring and hoses hang disconnected from the top of the engine, not mounted in a hull or test stand.
A round emblem/badge is visible on the side of the block but no legible text or serial/model plate can be read.
Surrounding yard items (green machinery frame, white cylindrical tank, other metal equipment) suggest a scrapyard or dealer storage yard, not an active vessel.
No gauges, control panel, or running indication visible; no video or startup evidence provided.

claims.evidence: No legible nameplate, serial tag, or model marking visible in photo 0; the round badge on the block is illegible at this resolution.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (common for long-stored, rusted engines).
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine starting, idling, and running under load.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for parts

risks.risk: Extent of rust and corrosion on internal components (cylinders, crankshaft) is unknown.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder bores, oil dipstick, and crankcase interior.

risks.risk: Engine may be missing key accessories (turbocharger, alternator, injectors, starter).
risks.proof: Multiple close-up photos from all sides showing completeness of accessories.

risks.risk: Model and specification (e.g., actual Detroit 6-71 vs. a different or rebadged unit) cannot be confirmed.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine's data/ID plate with serial and model number.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unidentified used diesel engine, not a confirmed Detroit 6-71

risks.risk: Usage history and hours are unknown, affecting remaining service life.
risks.proof: Hour meter photo or maintenance/service records.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine's ID/data plate showing make, model, and serial number.
Video of the engine being started and run, showing smoke, sound, and gauge readings if available.
Close-up photos of cylinder bores, oil condition, and crankcase interior.
Full set of photos from all four sides showing presence/absence of turbocharger, alternator, starter, and injectors.
Any maintenance logs or hour-meter reading.
response.reason: The item is clearly a large marine-type diesel engine, so it can be priced at its worst case (unverified running condition, unverified model, visible rust) as an as-is used industrial diesel engine, pending the seller's nameplate and running-condition proof to raise the valuation.
